meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
Then you've just told me you decided first and asked questions later. Who made that decision, Hale, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
I'm writing down October 15, and a line you say isn't in Hamlet. Which line, and do you have both documents here so I can read them myself?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: she stayed at her opening position, with the zero withdrawn, and agreed to nothing.
What moved her: "Let me show you what I actually have" got her to stop attacking and ask to read the documents, though she gave no ground on the zero because nothing had been shown yet.
What cost ground: "The zero stands." confirmed her view that the decision came first and the questions later, and it cost you the opening.
Try next time: open by owning in one sentence that the zero was entered before you called her, then put the dated documents in front of her instead of describing them.
